content: LIFE IN THE NEIGHBOURHOOD & CITY & SOCIAL LIFE

Sub-themes: ''Activities to do in attractions (cafes, cinemas; gyms, sports clubs); getting help from services (pharmacies, hospitals, etc.); pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):
Transportation: A bus, a train, a bike / bicycle, a taxi, on foot, a car, an aeroplane (air-plane-AmE).
Vocabulary for activities to do in attractions and recreational places in the neighbourhood and city (cafes, cinemas; gyms, sports clubs):
Verbs: To surf the Net, to chill out, to buy popcorn/ snacks, to attend fitness classes, to join tournaments, to do Pilates.
Vocabulary for getting help from services in the neighbourhood and the city (pharmacies, hospitals etc):
Nouns: A first-aid kit, a bandage. Verbs: To buy medicine, to ask for advice, to buy health products/ vitamins, to check blood pressure, to attend check-ups, to browse (in a chemist’s)
Vocabulary for pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city:
Transportation: Nouns: Public transport, an underground (subway- AmE), a ferry, a motorbike, a tram, a ship, a lorry (truck-AmE), e-scooters.
Pros and cons: Adjectives: Eco-friendly, reliable, efficient, affordable, convenient, time-saving, timeconsuming, polluting, unsafe, uncomfortable, (prone to) delays.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-The Past Progressive Tense: (I was going to the school by bike yesterday morning. I was going to school on foot while you were taking the bus last morning.)
-The Simple Past Tense vs Past Progressive Tense: (The doctor was checking my blood pressure when you called me.)
-Question tags: (You came to school on foot yesterday, didn’t you? There wasn’t a traffic jam two hours ago, was there?)
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".

*(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use:

Use of the Past Progressive Tense: Describing an action or other actions that are in progress in the past. Use of The Simple Past Tense vs Past Progressive Tense: Contrasting a completed action at specified time in the past with an action in progress at an exact moment in the past.
Use of Question Tags for The Simple Past Tense & The Past Progressive Tense: Confirming or clarifying past events.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
I need to pop to the market!
This city is full of cool sights!
Let’s catch the bus!
What a traffic jam!
The Topkapı Palace is a must-see in İstanbul!”
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Vowel: o: (/əʊ/, /ɒ/, /əʊ/)
Consonants: m (/ɛm/,/m/); n: (/ɛn/, /n/); p: ( /piː//p/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)

content: LIFE IN THE WORLD & CULTURE
Sub-themes: ''Continents, countries, and nationalities; shopping for food and personal food preferences; food and food culture from different parts of the world''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):
Vocabulary for countries and nationalities:
Countries (revisional): Türkiye, (UK) United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, Northen Ireland), France, Azerbaijan, Germany, Greece, Italy, Spain, China, Japan, Russia, India.
Nationalities (revisional): Turkish, British (English, Scottish, Welsh, Irish), French, Azerbaijani/Azeri, German, Greek, Italian, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Russian, Indian
Vocabulary for countries and nationalities:
Countries: Belgium, Croatia, Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Finland, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland, Egypt, Brazil, Argentina,
Nationalities: Belgian, Croatian, Turkish Cypriot, Czech, Danish, Finnish, Hungarian, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Swedish, Swiss, Egyptian, Brazilian, Argentinian.
Vocabulary for continents: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia, Oceans (The Pacific, Atlantic, Arctic, Indian, Southern). Verbs: to be surrounded.
Vocabulary for shopping for food and personal food preferences:

For shopping: A vegetarian, a vegan, a cashier, a shelf, a shop (store-AmE), a trolley (a cart-AmE), a receipt, a discount, a snack, a main course, a starter (an appetizer-AmE), traditional dishes, local dishes.
For preferences:

Healthy Food: Nouns: Garlic, grapes, mushroom. Unhealthy Food: Nouns: A burger, a biscuit (cookie-AmE), cereal, a dessert, French fries. Adjectives: Spicy, salty, bitter, sour, savoury (savory- AmE), fried, baked, grilled, gluten-free, dairy-free, sugar-free, halal, delicious, home-made.
Vocabulary for Food and Food culture from different parts of the world:
Nouns: Kebab, baklava (Türkiye), pasta, pizza, steak, falafel (Asian), sushi, chopsticks (Japan), croissant, chopsticks (French).
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".

*(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:

-The Present Perfect Tense (With how long, since, for, already, just) (How long have you been gluten-free? I have been gluten-free since I was sixteen.) (I have been to Ireland for six years. I have already ordered fast food. I have just bought some mushrooms.)
-Question Tags: (Türkiye is famous for its traditional dishes, isn’t it?) (You’ve eaten sushi before, haven’t you?)

-“Be able to” (Present, Past, Future, Perfect) (She is able to cook traditional dishes from Türkiye. They were able to find the shop despite the heavy rain. We will be able to buy the ingredients for the recipe tomorrow. I have been able to visit many countries this year.)

-Countable and Uncountable Nouns (Some, any, much, many): (She bought some vegetables from the market. Do you have any idea where the shop is? How much time do we have left? How many friends do you have in this city?)
-Need, needn’t for obligation (We need to buy some vegetables for dinner. She needn’t worry about the project, it’s already finished.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of the Present Perfect Tense: Describing actions that began in the past and continue into the present and describing an action that happened recently and has an impact on the present.
-Use of the “Question Tags”: Confirming information, encouraging agreement, seeking reassurance.
-Use of Countable Nouns and Uncountable Nouns: Describing an unspecified amount and uncertainty or absence, and expressing large quantities.
-Use of Modals “Need, Needn’t” for obligation: Describing that something is required or necessary or is not necessary or obligatory.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Do you want to grab a bite?
I’ll pick up a salad!
Let’s eat out tonight!
I’m not into spicy food!
Could you lend a hand for this?
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Consonants: q: /kjuː/, r: /ɑː/(Br), /r/ (AmE); , s: (/s/, /ɛs/, /z/); t : (/tiː/, /t/). *(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.).
keyConcepts: The target concept of this theme ''continents

and nationalities; shopping for food and personal food preferences; food and food culture from different parts of the world'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example
a student in an upper secondary school may know what ''continents

and nationalities; shopping for food and personal food preferences; food and food culture from different parts of the world'' mean but may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However
this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise
and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language
food and food culture from different parts of the world.

content: LIFE IN NATURE & GLOBAL PROBLEMS
Sub-themes: ''Natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary) :
Vocabulary for natural resources:
Nouns: Renewable resources, non-renewable resources, solar energy, wind energy, geothermal energy, freshwater, groundwater.
Vocabulary for global problems related to natural resources:

Nouns: Deforestation, soil pollution, habitat destruction, global warming, climate change, landslides, floods, loss of biodiversity, energy crisis, water shortage, overpopulation, urbanisation, industrialisation, poverty, carbon footprint, greenhouse gases, environmental problems.
Vocabulary for protecting natural resources:
Verbs: To use energy efficiently, to reduce consumption, to be environmentally conscious, to raise awareness, to take precautions, to reuse, to limit.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid alFitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".

*(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Defining Relative Clauses (that, which, who): (Renewable resources which include solar and wind energy are necessary for sustainable development.)
-Connecting Words (so…): (People need to take precautions, so they can protect wildlife from habitat destruction.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of Defining Relative clauses (that, which, who): Referring to people, objects or thingsto provide essential information.
-Use of connecting words (so…): Expressing cause and effect; explaining consequences.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
People need to take care of Mother nature’s bounty!
Our planet works like a well-oiled machine!
We’re at the tipping point with the loss of our ecosystem!
Let’s save our planet!
Let’s be green thumbs and plant trees!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Vowel: u: (/juː/, /ʌ/, /juː/)
Consonants: v: (/viː/, /v/); w: (/w/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)
keyConcepts: The target concept of this theme ''natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example

a student in an upper secondary school may know what ''natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources'' means but may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However
this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise
and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language
global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources

outcomes.text: can prepare and get ready for listening (to)/watching about the current content on ''life in nature and global problems with natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources''.
components: a) Students activate their pre-existing knowledge and experience about the current theme and content to recall their background knowledge by investigating it carefully.

b) Students identify significant and necessary relationships and connections between their pre-existing knowledge, their past experience and the clues to the current content by responding to meaningful questions about it (without speaking Turkish or using a translation).

outcomes.text: Students can bring together the information in the current content on ''life in nature and global problems with natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources''.
components: a) Students identify the main topic of the current content in general by listening (to)/watching it as a whole in its context.
b) Students recognise the significant details and basic components of the current content within the whole by listening (to) and watching the whole content carefully to notice them.

outcomes.text: Students can make sense of and derive meaning from the current content on ''life in nature and global problems with natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources''.
components: a) Students check their initial predictions about the current content by being aware of the commonalities between their self-predictions and the clues provided as visuals surrounding the content.
b) Students make significant and necessary classifications in the current content that affect the meaning of the generally perceived content.

c) Students make significant and necessary comparisons in the generally perceived current content to highlight differences between two or more different things by using visuals, ensuring clarity and meaning.

g) Students construct a detailed understanding of the meaning of the current content through prior classifications, comparisons, and inferences/deductions.
h) Students position, internalise and personalise current content in an individualised, age-appropriate and level-appropriate way.

outcomes.text: Students can reflect on the information, experiences, thoughts, ideas, and feelings related to the listening (to)/watching process about the current content on ''life in nature and global problems with natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources'' in relation to themselves or others, both individually and/or with others.
components: a) Students individually convey their personal knowledge, experiences, thoughts, and feelings that are critically reviewed in relation to the current listening (to)/watching contents and the process.

outcomes.text: Students can select and use target phonological aspects such as pronunciation and intonation of target sounds, words, phrases, clauses, and sentences in utterances authentically, naturally, and accurately in the current content about ''life in nature and global problems with natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources'' to develop holistic and conscious pronunciation skills after recognising them in context.
components: a) Students recognise the target phonological aspects such as pronunciation and intonation of target sounds, words, phrases and sentences in utterances within the current content by listening (to)/ watching it, first as a whole and then with pauses.

e) Students evaluate feedback from others and their personal feedback and reflection by listening to or watching the audio/visual content again to check for accuracy.

f)Students utilise the target phonological aspects such as pronunciation and intonation of utterances including target sounds of the current content, appropriately, effectively, accurately, naturally, automatically, and consciously when communicating with others in different contexts.

components: a) Students listen to, watch, and/or read the audio, visual, and written current content presented in context that introduces the general use of the target language structures in the current theme.

b) Students use appropriate discourse forms, styles, and strategies for the assigned (prepared and/or unprepared) writing task, considering its writing type and appropriate to their age and language level.

outcomes.text: Students can engage in the process of writing related to the content on ''life in nature and global problems with natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources''.
components: a) Students review the feedback from the teacher and/or peers critically on their prepared and/or unprepared writing task(s).
b) Students revise to reorganise the written content of their prepared and/or unprepared task based on the feedback received from the teacher and/or peers.

outcomes.text: Students can reconstruct their writing about the current theme on ''life in nature and global problems with natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources'' to communicate effectively about it.
components: a) Students adapt and use individually internalised information in current or similar content by selecting and reorganising it meaningfully in written form as necessary when communicating with other people in different contexts.
b) Students exchange information and ideas in written communication by sharing reconstructed meaningful knowledge and content with others.

outcomes.text: Students can reflect on their experiences, thoughts, ideas, and feelings related to the writing process about the current content on ''life in nature and global problems with natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources'' in relation to themselves or others, both individually and/or with others.
components: a) Students convey individually the knowledge, experiences, thoughts, and feelings they review critically in relation to their current writing-expression content and process.

b) Students share their personal verbal and written knowledge, experiences, thoughts, and feelings that they critically review in relation to the current writing-expression content and process with others.
c) Students produce their new verbal and written work after participating in reflective activities related to the current writing-expression content and process.

outcomes.text: Students can prepare themselves to speak meaningfully, fluently, and efficiently about the current content on ''life in nature and global problems with natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources''.
components: a) Students relate current content by analysing pre-existing knowledge and experiences from earlier listening, watching, and reading sessions to associate them with the current content.

outcomes.text: Students can analyse and understand the model content related to ''life in nature and global problems with natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources'' to support the production of spoken language.
components: a) Students grasp what the provided model/example is about with the help of audio, visual, and/or written elements after listening, watching, and/or reading the current content.

outcomes.text: Students can produce meaningful and accurate spoken content related to the current theme on ''life in nature and global problems with natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources''.
components: a) Students recognise which form and type of spoken content is expected and assigned based on the model/example about the current theme for both prepared and/or unprepared speaking situations through careful examination.
b) Students conduct preliminary research on the expected and assigned content to be produced for prepared and/or unprepared speaking situations.

c) Students develop a draft outline in accordance with the assigned prepared and/or unprepared speaking situations as presented in the model/example, appropriate to the age and language level based on the current theme.

d) Students organise supplementary audio-visual materials in accordance with the assigned task as presented in the model/example for prepared and/or unprepared speaking situations and appropriate to their age and language level.
e) Students organise information related to the current content to be presented, appropriate to the model/example for prepared and/or unprepared speaking situations.
f) Students critically review their prepared presentation content for accuracy, coherence, and appropriateness to audience and context in prepared and/or unprepared speaking situations.

outcomes.text: Students can construct meaningful spoken content about ''life in nature and global problems with natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources'' through efficient and meaningful practice.
components: a) Students make spoken content clear and understandable to listeners by selecting and using style and form appropriate to age and language level in prepared and/or unprepared speaking situations.

b) Students present their spoken content by selecting and using materials appropriate to the context, age, language level, style, and type of discourse, similar to those presented in the model/example for prepared and/or unprepared speaking situations.

c) Students present their spoken content by selecting and using target vocabulary and language structures similar and/or appropriate to those presented in the model/example considering their age, language level, context, style, and type of discourse for prepared and/or unprepared speaking situations.

d) Students convey relevant explicit, implicit, and/or complex messages related to the current content clearly in context to the listeners by using appropriate material and body language in prepared and/or unprepared speaking situations.
e) Students convey their messages about the current content clearly to the listeners by incorporating all the necessary semantic elements in prepared and/or unprepared speaking situations.

outcomes.text: Students can reconstruct the information about ''life in nature and global problems with natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources'' when communicating with others.
components: a) Students use the same or similar information presented in the current content in verbal or written forms in different contexts by reorganising it meaningfully, accurately, effectively, efficiently, functionally, and individually as required.
b) Students engage in verbal and/or written communication by sharing the reconstructed meaningful information about the current content with others.

content: LIFE IN THE UNIVERSE & THE FUTURE
Sub-themes: ''Planets and space; life in the universe; space explorations''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):
Vocabulary for planets and space:

Planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. Nouns: Universe, galaxy, Milky Way, solar system, satellite, a meteor, an asteroid, a comet, an orbit, to revolve, Adjective: Celestial.
Vocabulary for life in the universe:
Nouns: Atmosphere, a robot, a creature, a space colony, Adjectives: tiny, unknown, weird. mysterious, rare. Vocabulary for space explorations:

Nouns: Space travel, space mission, telescope, an astronaut, a spacecraft, a rocket, a space shuttle, a space capsule Verbs: to launch, to take off, to land, to collect data, to conduct experiments, to go on a spacewalk
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".

*(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Zero Conditional: (If you go to the Moon, everything floats in space. If a planet is in orbit, it travels around a star.)
-Conditional 1: (If you want to explore space, you can become an astronaut.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
Use of the Zero Conditional: Describing general and/or scientific facts which are generally true.
Use of the Conditional 1: Describing a possible future situation.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
It’s a small world!
She’s so strange, she is definitely not from this planet!
A star is born!
This is a whole new world!
It felt like being a man on the moon!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Consonants: x: (/ɛks/, /ks/, /gz/); y: (/waɪ//waɪ//waɪ/, /j/, /ɪ/, /iː/); z: /zed/ (Br), /ziː/ (AmE), /z/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)

units.theme: Upper Secondary-Year 10 (After Prep)-Level: B2.2 - Theme 1: School Lıfe & Educatıon
content: SCHOOL LIFE & EDUCATION
Sub-themes: "School problems and challenges for students; role of parents in education; purpose of education; national days and celebrations"
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):

Vocabulary for school problems: Nouns: Accuracy, confusion, a penalty, an obstacle, an obligation, an assessment, a disability, motivation. Verbs: To permit, to forbid, to interrupt, to distract, to fail, to evaluate, to restrict, to grade. Adjectives: Strict, isolated.
Adverbs: Adequately, barely, accurately.
Vocabulary for challenges for students in education: Nouns: Concentration, interruption, a failure, a conflict, bias, an expectation, an addiction, an assessment, a deadline.

Phrases: A learning disability, lack of motivation, an attention span, a language barrier, a low self-esteem, a conflict resolution, time management. Verbs: To disturb, to struggle, to exclude, to overcome, to cope, to submit. Adjectives: Abstract, aggressive, complicated, concerned, confusing.
Vocabulary for role of parents in education: Nouns: A fund, assistance, a facility.
Verbs: To accompany, to approve, to motivate. Adverbs: Permanently.
Vocabulary for purpose of education: Nouns: A certificate, academic, literacy, finance, leadership, creativity.
Adjectives: Accurate, actual, capable, professional. Verbs: To assure, to gain, to acquire, to inform, to assign.
Adverbs: Precisely.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:

-The Present Tenses Used for Narration (The Simple Present Tense, the Present Progressive Tense, the Present Perfect Tense, the Present Perfect Progressive Tense): (The school has provided additional support to students with learning disabilities).

- ''Be Used to'' in All Present Tenses: (She is used to studying until late hours). -Get Used to'' in All Present Tenses: (Many students get used to academic pressure after studying so hard). (I’m used to studying very hard).
-Conjunctions (As soon as, still, so far, not only, whatsoever): (As soon as you receive a certificate, you can apply for better jobs).
-Complex Question Tags: (You haven’t had any obstacles in your classroom, have you?)
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:

-Use of The Present Tenses Used for Narration (The Simple Present Tense, the Present Progressive Tense, the Present Perfect Tense, the Present Perfect Progressive Tense): Narrating an action that is occurring at the time or happened in the past.

-Use of ''Be used to'' in Present Tenses: Describing being familiar and/or comfortable with thing since they are not new to that person anymore. -Use of ''Get used to'' in all Present Tenses: Describing the process of having habits and getting accustomed to them.
-Use of Conjunctions (As soon as, still, so far, not only, whatsoever): Linking the actions or ideas.
-Use of Complex Question Tags: Expressing verification or confirmation.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
They need to hit the books.
Back to school, back to growth!
Your future is written in today’s effort.
Success speaks in flying colours!
Burn the midnight oil, shine all day!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
-Intonation for positive statements, negative statements, questions, and question tags.
keyConcepts: The target concept of this theme ''school life and education with its components such as school problems; challenges for students role of parents in education; purpose of education; national days and celebrations'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example

a student in year 10 of upper secondary school may know what ''school life and education with its components such as school problems; challenges for students role of parents in education; purpose of education; national days and celebrations'' means
but may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However
this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise
and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language

content: CLASSROOM LIFE & LEARNING
Sub-themes: "Innovations in education and learning; personal ways and strategies of learning; study habits''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):

Vocabulary for innovations in education and learning: Nouns: An asset, an integration, globalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), creativity. Verbs: To enable, to alter, to boost. Adjectives: Critical, interactive, technological. Phrases: Digital literacy, lifelong learning, self-paced learning, learning apps, mobile learning, smart classrooms, user-friendly, digital tools, distance learning. Vocabulary for personal ways and strategies of learning: Nouns: An observation, a visual, an approach, a concept, inference. Verbs: To associate, to assume, to brainstorm, to classify, to engage, to clarify, to debate, to demonstrate, to emphasize, to illustrate, to infer, to summarise. Phrases: Visual/auditory/kinaesthetic/ social/solitary learning. Adjectives: Efficient. Adverbs: Briefly, broadly. Vocabulary for study habits: Nouns: Note-taking, mind mapping, revision. Verbs: To advance, to evaluate, to chart. Phrases: Problem-solving, critical thinking, goal setting, taking a break, self-assessment. Adjectives: Disciplined, detailed.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”.

*(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Passive Voice for Present Tenses: (The assignment is completed by the students every evening. English is taught in a lot of schools around the world. Dinner is being prepared by the cook now).
- ''Shall'' for Suggestions: (Shall we try using a new app to organise our study programme? Shall I help you organise a quiet study environment at home?)
-''Have got to'' and ''Ought to'' for Obligation: (I have got to finish the presentation by Thursday).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of Passive Voice for Present Tenses: Describing actions, events, and/or processes where the focus is on the activity or outcome, rather than the person performing it at present times.
-Use of Passive Words with Two Objects: (I was given an assignment by the teacher).
-Use of ''Shall'' for Suggestions: Proposing ideas or seeking agreement to make suggestions.
-Use of ''Have got to'' and ''Ought to'' for Obligation: Expressing a moral or logical obligation, advice, or recommendation.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Every class is a step forward.
No shortcuts in learning!
Make mistakes.
That’s how you learn!
Ask questions.
Own answers!
Learn hard, lead harder!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
-Intonation for positive statements, negative statements, questions, and question tags.
keyConcepts: The target concept of this theme ''classroom life and learning with its components such as innovations in education and learning; personal ways and strategies of learning; study habits'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example

a student in year 10 of upper secondary school may know what ''classroom life and learning with its components such as innovations in education and learning; personal ways and strategies of learning; study habits'' means
but may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However
this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise
and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language

Sub-themes: "Planning life-time personal well-being; personal choices and preferences for sports and extreme sports; personal choices for films and film genres; music and music genres''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):

Vocabulary for planning life-time personal well-being: Nouns: Mind-set, adaptability, passion, self-reflection, a purpose, stress, an approach, awareness, value, fear, vision, achievement, satisfaction, a priority, a deadline, a balance, a barrier, measurement, an outline, commitment, an influence, a requirement, a therapist. Verbs: to outline, to reflect, to achieve, to overcome, to adjust, to ensure, to gain, to bear, to measure, to commit, to accompany, to influence. Adjectives: Beneficial, unacceptable, urgent, essential, complicated, challenging, satisfied, balanced, core, relevant, flexible. Adverbs: Steadily, adequately, essentially, firmly. Word groups:
To break down, to set up, to take up, to do for a living, to keep in mind, to go through.
Vocabulary for extreme sports across earth: Nouns: Free climbing.
Vocabulary for extreme sports across water: Nouns: Kite surfing, kiteboarding, cave diving, free diving, sailing.
Vocabulary for extreme sports across snow and ice: Nouns: Ice climbing, snow kiting. Vocabulary for extreme sports across air: Nouns: Base jumping.

Vocabulary for personal choices and preferences for sports and extreme sports: Nouns: determination, a helmet, a marathon, a medal, oxygen, panic, suffering, patience, preference, a scratch, survival, a territory, a capacity, a current, courage, confidence, desire, discipline, enthusiasm, freedom.

Verbs: To favour, to challenge, to crack, to dare, to devote, to equip, to scratch, to strengthen, to drag, to inspire. Adjectives: Bold, deadly, memorable, overseas, passionate, relieved, capable, enthusiastic, fellow.
Vocabulary for films and film genres: Nouns: Fantasy, horror, cast, budget, an origin.
Vocabulary for types of music and music genres: Nouns: A tone, rhythm, a lyric, a gig.

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”.

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. Target Grammatical Structures in Use:

-The Past Tenses for Narration (The Simple Past Tense, the Past Progressive Tense, the Past Perfect Tense, the Past Perfect Progressive Tense): (He had followed the guideline for his fitness routine before he saw the results).

units.theme: Upper Secondary-Year 10 (After Prep)-Level: B2.2 - Theme 4: Famıly Lıfe & Home
content: FAMILY LIFE & HOME
Sub-themes: "Designing and decorating family homes; housing problems and family conflicts; family traditions and customs about food''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):

Vocabulary for designing and decorating family homes: Nouns: A household, a layout, lighting, decoration, maintenance, a storage, renovation, a porch, veranda (patio AmE.), a basement, convenience, a collector, a hallway (corridor-AmE), a counter, an extension, a hook, a deck, litter (trash-AmE), patience. Verbs: To accommodate, to purchase, to equip, to restore, to rebuild, to collapse. Adjectives: Affordable, concrete, conventional, genuine, adequate, mechanical, domestic, inner, thorough, functional, aesthetically pleasing, decent. Vocabulary for housing problems: Verbs: To ruin, to spoil, to collapse. Phrases: Rising material cost, high land cost, a lack of skilled construction workers, use of cheaper and lower-quality material, out-dated construction methods, poor quality control. Vocabulary for family conflicts: Nouns: Tension, a separation, rejection, suspicion, privacy, a remark, a debt. Verbs: To deny, to criticise, to reject, to restrict, to interrupt, to offend, to oppose, to suspect, to tear, to urge, to cancel. Vocabulary for family traditions and customs about food: Nouns: Harvest meal, teatime, cultural cuisine, a special occasion. Verbs: To honour, to praise, to satisfy, Adverbs: Thoroughly.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:

-Comparative and Superlative Adjectives (Regular-Irregular Forms): (This house is more affordable than the one in the town. The decoration in the study room is the most elegant decoration in the house).
-Same as, the same: (Jane gets the same salary as me. You’re just the same as your mother).
-As... as: (Mehmet isn’t as old as he looks).
-Like, alike, slightly: (You look like your father. My siblings look alike. My brother is slightly taller than me).
- ''Cleft Sentences'' with Adjectives: (What you did for this house is wonderful).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of Comparative and Superlative Adjectives: Expressing the degrees of differences.
-Use of Same as, the same: Expressing similarity or equality.
-Use of As... as: Emphasizing the degree of similarity.
-Use of Like, alike, slightly: Expressing slight differences.
-Use of ''Cleft Sentences'' with Adjectives: Emphasising a particular part of a sentence to emphasise an idea, fact, situation.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Home is not a place, it’s a feeling.
Together is our favourite place to be.
Every family has a story - welcome to ours!
Family is the anchor in the storm.
A happy home is built with kindness.
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Vowels: a, e
Consonants: b, c, d
Vowels: a: (/ae/, /aeı/, /ə/, /a:/, /eɪ/, /a:/, /a/, /ɔː/, /eə/); e: (/e/; /i:/, /ə/, silent /e/)
Consonant: b: (/b/), silent /b/); c: (/si/, /k/, /tʃ/, /z/, silent /c/); d: (/d/), silent /d/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme).

units.theme: Upper Secondary-Year 10 (After Prep)-Level: B2.2 - Theme 5: Lıfe In The Neıghbourhood, Cıty & Socıal Lıfe
content: LIFE IN THE NEIGHBOURHOOD, CITY AND SOCIAL LIFE

Sub-themes: ''Lifestyles and culture on leisure activities in the neighbourhood and city; urban trends and technology; performing arts (dance, theatre) and visual arts (painting, sculpture, architecture) in the city''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):

Vocabulary for lifestyles and culture on leisure activities in the neighbourhood and city: Nouns: A stall, a resident, a consequence, preservation, promotion, appreciation, construction, an aspect, mobility. Verbs: To unite, to hold, to appreciate, to perceive, to contribute, to comfort, to declare. Adjectives: Constant, vital, crucial, historical, contemporary, overall, fundamental, concerned. Vocabulary for urban trends: Nouns: Urbanisation. Phrases: Urban farming, affordable housing, green spaces, smart lighting, eco-cities, city planning, public art. Phrases for technology in the city: Self-driving cars, robotics, a solar panel, a wind farm, a recycling facility, an urban farming. Vocabulary for performing arts (dance, theatre): Nouns: Artwork, a ballet, a performance, a script, a venue, a production, costume, a stage. Verbs: To act, to rehearse, to stage, to interpret, to host, to house. Adjectives: Artistic, iconic, expressive, captivating. Vocabulary for visual arts (Painting, Sculpture, Photography, Architecture): Nouns: A canvas, a gallery, a portrait, a composition, pattern, concrete, steel, murals. Verbs: To craft, to photograph, to capture, to illustrate, to compose, to construct, to visualize. Adjectives: Abstract, contemporary, historic, inspiring.

*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations: “29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:

-Passive Voice for Past Tenses: (A local festival was organized in the city center last weekend. A famous play was performed at the theatre last night. The sculptures were being displayed at the city’s art gallery last month).
-Causatives: (to have someone do something; to have something done (Passive)): (We had the guide show the place). (The gallery had the photographs framed for the upcoming exhibit).
-''Be Able to'' in Past Tenses and the Present Perfect Tenses: (The artist was able to finish the sculpture before the exhibition opening). Functions of the
Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of Passive Voice for/in Past Tenses: Describing actions or events in the past where the focus is on the outcome or what happened, rather than who performed the action.
-Use of Causatives: (to have someone do something (active); to have something done): Describing situations arranged for someone to perform a task or service.
-Use of ''Be able to'' in/for Past Tenses and Present Perfect Tenses: Describing ability for completed actions and continuation or the result of this ability over time.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Be the neighbour you wish to have!
Strangers are just friends you haven’t met yet!
Every street has a story!
Cities grow but culture holds them together!
Walk the block, meet the world!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Vowels: i: (/aı/, /ı/, /i:/)
Consonants: f: (/f/); g: (/g/, /dʒ/, silent /g/); h: (/h/), silent /h/); j: (/dʒeɪ/, /dʒ/); k: (/k/, silent /k/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme).

units.theme: Upper Secondary-Year 10 (After Prep)-Level: B2.2 - Theme 6: Lıfe In The World & Culture
content: LIFE IN THE WORLD & CULTURE
Sub-themes: "Media and popular culture, celebrities and influencers; global influence of films, music and fashion on culture and lifestyles; cross-cultural communication''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):

Vocabulary for media and popular culture, celebrities and influencers: Nouns: An attachment, an affair, an animation, a broadcaster, fame, journalism, an icon, an illustration, a preference, popularity, publishing, a sponsorship, a tendency, reputation, exposure, publicity, rating. Verbs: To demand, to expose, to praise, to satisfy, to select, to sponsor. Adjectives: Characteristic, charming, dominant, editorial, elegant, enjoyable, entertaining, fond, lively, widespread, willing. Vocabulary for global influence of films, music and fashion on culture and lifestyles: Nouns: A composer, contribution, creation, a critic, delight, a genre, a scenario, a screening, a tale, a choir. Verbs: To broadcast, to compose, to criticise, to display, to inspire, to rate. Adjectives: Comic, classic, dramatic, fake, humorous, intellectual, prime. Vocabulary for multicultural societies: Nouns: A majority, a minority, a representative, a combination, interaction, a viewpoint. Verbs: To integrate, to adopt, to differ. Adjectives: Regional, diverse.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”.

*(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-The Future Progressive Tense: (During the awards ceremony, the reporters will be interviewing actors on the red carpet).
-''Will get used to'': (People will get used to using translation apps to understand foreign languages in the future).

-Passive Voice for/in Future Tenses: (The new TV series will be released next month on a national TV channel. By the end of this decade, many important technological developments will have been achieved).
-Complex Question Tags: (I’m becoming more familiar with global music trends, aren’t I?)
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of the Future Progressive Tense: Describing actions or events that will be happening at a particular time in the future by emphasising ongoing activity or progression.
-Use of ''Will get used to'': Expressing how someone will adapt or become accustomed to new habits, situations, or environments over time in the future.
-Use of Passive Voice for/in Future Tenses: Describing future events or actions where the focus is on the outcome or the object of the action rather than the person or entity performing it.
-Use of Complex Question Tags: Confirming information, checking understanding, and/ or seeking agreement in complex sentence structures or with varying verb forms and auxiliaries.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Culture is how we tell our stories!
Creativity connects more than borders do!
One world, many wonders!
The more you see, the more you grow!
Explore. Connect. Respect!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Vowel: o
Consonants: l, m, n, (ng), p
Vowel: o: (/əʊ/, /ɒ/) Consonants: l: (/ɛl/ /l/, silent /l/); m; (/ɛm/,/m/); n: (/ɛn/, /n/, silent /n/); ng: (/ng/); p: (piː//p/, silent /p/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme).

content: LIFE IN NATURE & GLOBAL PROBLEMS
Sub-themes: "Sustainable development (eco-friendly buildings, green technology); food security and famine; climate change and its global impact: problems and solutions''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):

Vocabulary for sustainable development: Nouns: Agriculture, carbon, conservation, biodiversity, reduction, protection. Verbs: To maintain, to convert, to generate, to preserve, to promote. Adjectives: Solar, urban, harmful, sustainable, biological. Adverbs: Efficiently, entirely, sufficiently. Vocabulary for food security and famine: Nouns: Awareness, consumption, nutrition, malnutrition, a shortage, a distribution, a source. Verbs: To distribute, to ensure, to modify, to secure, to starve, to supply. Adjectives: Adequate, affordable, artificial, balanced, extreme, imbalanced, reasonable, rural. Adverbs: Adequately, deeply. Vocabulary for climate change and its global impact: Nouns: Problems and solutions: acid rain, carbon footprint, deforestation, emission, warming, a glacier, a spread, extinction, awareness, transportation, species, tragedy. Verbs: To absorb, to conserve, to release, to melt, to threaten, to pose, to undertake, to impose, to abuse, to exploit. Adjectives: Renewable, severe, tragic. Adverbs: Additionally. Idioms: To pose a threat, to become extinct.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:

-Defining and Non-defining Relative Pronouns Used for Relative Clauses (whose, whom, where, when, which): (The farmer whose crops were destroyed by the heavy rains is looking for financial aid. The village, where the drought is particularly severe, has been receiving international aid). -Forming Nouns from Verbs Using -ing (swim - swimming, play – playing): (Conserving natural resources like forests can help cope with deforestation and its harmful effects). -Verb + object + gerund (-ing form) (verbs: stop, prevent, keep, dislike, catch): (The doctor prevented the patient from taking the wrong medicine).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:

-Use of Defining and Non-defining Relative Pronouns Used for Relative Clauses (whose, whom, where, when, whose, o which): Giving information or extra information about the subject or object mentioned.

-Use of Forming Nouns from Verbs Using -ing (swim - swimming, play – playing): Turning actions or processes into concepts. -Use of verb + object + gerund (-ing form) (verbs: stop, prevent, keep): Describing prevention, experience, and involvement, etc.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
The earth is speaking—are we listening?
Live simply, so nature can simply live!
Pollution is silent, but deadly!
Let nature be your teacher!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Vowel: u
Consonants: q, r, s, t
Vowel: u: (/juː/, /ʌ/, silent /u/)
Consonants: q: (/kjuː/, /k/); r: (/ɑː/(Br), silent /r/ (Br), /aɹ/ (AmE), /ɹ/ (AmE), silent /r/ (Br)); s: (/s/, /ɛs/, /z/, silent /s/); t : (/tiː/, /t/, silent /t/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme).
keyConcepts: The target concept of this theme ''sustainable development (eco-friendly buildings

green technology); food security and famine; climate change and its global impact: problems and solutions'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example
a student in year 10 of upper secondary school may know what ''sustainable development (eco-friendly buildings
green technology); food security and famine; climate change and its global impact: problems and solutions'' means
but may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However
this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise
and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language
problems and solutions of climate change.

content: LIFE IN THE UNIVERSE & THE FUTURE
Sub-themes: "The development of space travel technologies (rockets, spacecrafts); the concept of space tourism and its future; science fiction and imagination''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):

Vocabulary for the development of space travel technologies (rockets, space crafts): Nouns: Means, a mission, a rocket, an innovation. Verbs: To abandon, to launch, to revolutionise. Adjectives: Astonishing, innovative, distant. Adverbs: Upwards. Vocabulary for the concept of space tourism and its future: Nouns: An assumption, a prospect, a crew, advancement, an investment, safety, an excursion, a probability. Verbs: To emerge, to conduct, to book. Adjectives: Commercial, lunar, unique, potential. Vocabulary for science fiction and imagination: Nouns: A fantasy, a genre, inspiration, a vision. Verbs: To simulate, to inspire. Adjectives: Extraordinary, impressed, fictional.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Background Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of the Conditional 2: Describing an imaginary or unreal situation in the present and future.
*About “Background Grammatical Structures in Use”:

The “Background Grammatical Structures” in this section are not only revisional but also serve as contextual support and contribute to meaning-making. They are intended to be used within the theme to help students grasp the meaning of the language constructed through the use of “Target Grammatical Structures” without being explicitly taught. These structures are not considered “Target Grammatical Structures” themselves rather they function as a part of the facilitation process, supporting both the target forms and the contexts in which they are used. They provide opportunities for learning through revised and scaffolded language.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Conditional 2: (If people made a significant innovation in fuel technology, space travel would be more affordable).
-Conditional 3: (If people had made a significant innovation in fuel technology, space travel would have become more affordable)
-Modals in the Past (Could, Would, May, Should, Ought to, Might, Must have + past participle): ''You could have been more careful about the warnings''.

- ''Wish'' (Present, Past, Future): I wish I was on a spaceship (Present Unreal situation). I wish I had learnt more about space (Past regret). I wish you would help me with my assignment about space (Complaint-Future).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of Conditional 3: Describing imaginary situations (which did not happen) in the past.
-Use of Modals in the Past: Expressing possibility, advice, necessity, ability, expectation and criticism in relation to the past.
-Use of ''Wish'' (for the Present and Future): Expressing wishes, regrets, desires and unreal situations about the present or future.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Innovation starts with a question!
The future belongs to the curious!
Tomorrow is written by today’s dreamers!
Our future is written in the stars!
The universe doesn’t wait for us to catch up!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Consonants: v, w, x, y, z
Consonants: v: (/viː/, /v/); w: (/w/), silent /w/); x: (/ɛks/, /ks/, /gz/); y: (/waɪ/, /j/, /ɪ/, /iː/); z: /(zed/ (Br), /ziː/ (AmE), /z/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme).
keyConcepts: The target concept of this theme ''life in the universe and the future with its components such as the development of space travel technologies (rockets

spacecrafts); the concept of space tourism and its future; science fiction and imagination'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example

a student in the year 10 (after prep) of an upper secondary school may know what ''life in the universe and the future with its components such as the development of space travel technologies (rockets
spacecrafts); the concept of space tourism and its future; science fiction and imagination'' means
but may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However
this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise
and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language

units.subject: Kimya
content: Kimyasal Tepkimeler: Kimyasal Değişimin Göstergeleri, Kimyasal Tepkimelerin Oluşumu, Kimyasal Tepkime Türleri, Mol Kavramı, Kimyasal Tepkime Denklemlerinin Denkleştirilmesi, Kimyasal (Stokiyometrik) Hesaplamalar
Gazlar: Gazların Özellikleri ve Kinetik Moleküler Teori, Gaz Yasaları, İdeal Gaz Yasası, Graham Difüzyon ve Efüzyon Yasası

outcomes.text: Kimyasal değişimlere ilişkin kanıtları belirlemeye yönelik bilimsel gözlem yapabilme
components: a) Kimyasal değişimlerin gözlemlenebilir göstergelerini (enerji değişimi, gaz çıkışı, renk değişimi veya yeni bir katının oluşumu) tanımlar.
b) Kimyasal değişimlerin gözlemlenebilir göstergelerine ilişkin veri toplar ve kaydeder.
c) Kimyasal değişimlerin gözlemlenebilir göstergelerine ilişkin topladığı verileri tepkenlerin alt mikro seviyedeki değişimi temelinde açıklar.

outcomes.text: Kimyasal tepkimelerin oluşumunu açıklamak için bilimsel model oluşturabilme
components: a)Taneciklerin yeniden düzenlenmesi temelinde kimyasal tepkimelerin oluşumu için önerdiği modeli farklı kimyasal tepkimelerin oluşum süreçlerini inceleyerek sınar.
b) Sınama sürecinde elde ettiği kanıtlara uygun olarak modelini geliştirir.

outcomes.text: Kimyasal tepkime türlerinin oluşum sürecine ilişkin bilimsel gözlem yapabilme
components: a) Tepkime türlerinin (çökelme, indirgenme-yükseltgenme, asit-baz) oluşum sürecine ilişkin gözlemlenebilir göstergeleri (renk değişimi, çökelek oluşumu, enerji değişimi, gaz çıkışı) tanımlar.
b) Tepkime türlerinin oluşum sürecine ilişkin gözlemlenebilir göstergelere yönelik veri toplar ve kaydeder.
c) Tepkimelerin oluşum sürecine ilişkin verileri sembolik ve alt mikro seviyedeki gösterimlerle açıklar.

outcomes.text: Mol kavramına ilişkin operasyonel tanımlama yapabilme
components: a) Maddelerin miktarını ifade etmek için ölçülebilir (kütle, tanecik sayısı vb.) özellikleri belirler.
b) Maddelerin aynı sayıda tanecik içeren örneklerinin kütlesini ölçer.
c) Maddelerin tanecik sayısını ifade etmek için yaptığı işlemlere uygun tanım yapar.

outcomes.text: Saf maddelerin ölçülebilir özellikleri arasındaki ilişkileri belirlemeye yönelik tümdengelimsel akıl yürütebilme
components: a) Atom sayısı, molekül sayısı, kütle ile mol sayısı arasındaki ilişkiyi kuramsal temele dayalı kurduğu hipotezleri ile test eder.
b) Değişkenler arasındaki orantısal ilişkilere yönelik hipotezlerini yeni durumları açıklamak için kullanır.

outcomes.text: Kimyasal tepkime denklemlerinde tanecik sayılarının tutarsızlıklarına ilişkin çelişkiyi giderebilme
components: a) Kimyasal tepkime denklemlerinde tepken ve ürünlerin tanecik sayılarındaki tutarsızlıkların nerede olduğunu belirler.
b) Kimyasal tepkime denklemlerinde tepken ve ürünlerin tanecik sayılarının denkleştirilmesi için olası yolları araştırır.
c) Kimyasal tepkime denklemlerinde tepken ve ürünlerin tanecik sayılarının denkleştirilmesi için uygun yolu seçerek uygular.
ç) Kimyasal tepkime denklemlerinde tanecik sayılarının denkliğini değerlendirir.

outcomes.text: Kimyasal tepkimelerde stokiyometrik ilişkilere yönelik tümdengelimsel akıl yürütebilme
components: a) Denkleştirilmiş kimyasal tepkimelerde tepken ve ürünlerin katsayıları ile mol sayıları arasındaki ilişkileri belirler.
b) Denkleştirilmiş kimyasal tepkimelerde tepken ve ürünler arasındaki stokiyometrik ilişkileri kurar.
c) Denkleştirilmiş kimyasal tepkimelerde tepken ve ürünler arasındaki stokiyometrik ilişkilere yönelik çıkarım yapar.

outcomes.text: Gazların özelliklerine ilişkin bilimsel gözlem yapabilme
components: a) Gazların özelliklerinin (hacim, basınç, genleşme, sıkıştırılabilirlik, karışabilirlik, yoğunluk) farkını ortaya koyar.
b) Gazların özelliklerine ilişkin veri toplar ve kaydeder.
c) Topladığı veriler üzerinden gazların özelliklerine (basınç, hacim, sıcaklık ve madde miktarı) ilişkin keşfettiği örüntüleri tanecikli model ile açıklar.

outcomes.text: Gazların özellikleri arasındaki ilişkileri bilimsel sorgulayabilme
components: a) Gazların hacim, basınç, sıcaklık ve madde miktarı değişkenleri arasındaki ilişkilere yönelik araştırılabilir sorular oluşturur.
b) Değişkenler arasındaki ilişkiyi belirlemek üzere hipotez kurar.
c) Basınç, hacim, sıcaklık ve madde miktarı arasındaki ikili ilişkileri gösteren gaz yasalarına yönelik araştırma planlar ve planladığı araştırmayı gerçekleştirir.
ç) Çizdiği grafikler üzerinden matematiksel modeller önerir.
d) Elde ettiği grafiksel ve matematiksel modelleri kullanarak gazlara ilişkin değişkenler (P, V, T,
n) arasındaki ilişkileri açıklar.
e) Gaz yasalarını kinetik moleküler teori ile değerlendirir.

outcomes.text: İdeal gaz denklemini tümevarımsal akıl yürütme yoluyla oluşturabilme
components: a) Boyle, Charles ve Avogadro yasaları arasında örüntü oluşturur.
b) Gazların basınç, hacim, sıcaklık ve mol sayısı değişkenleri arasındaki ilişkiyi genel matematiksel bir eşitlikle ifade eder.

outcomes.text: Gazların farklı ortamlarda yayılmasına ilişkin deney yapabilme
components: a) Efüzyon ve difüzyon ile ilgili deney tasarlar.
b) Deney sonuçlarını günlük hayattaki durumları açıklamak için kullanır.

content: Çözeltiler: Çözünme Süreci, Maddelerin Birbiri İçindeki Çözünebilirliği, Çözünme Olayının Sınıflandırılması, Çözünürlük, Çözünürlüğe Etki Eden Faktörler (Sıcaklık, Basınç ve Madde Cinsi), Çözeltilerin Sınıflandırılması, Derişim Birimleri (Molarite ve ppm), Koligatif Özellikler (Kaynama Noktası Yükselmesi ve Donma Noktası Düşmesi)

outcomes.text: Çözünme sürecine ilişkin bilimsel model oluşturabilme
