content: Uluslararası Birliktelik ve Anlaşmazlıklar
Ulaşım Sistemleri: Örnek Ülkeler
Ticari Faaliyetler: Örnek Ülke
Turizm Faaliyetleri: Örnek Ülkeler

outcomes.text: Uluslararası birlikteliklerin anlaşmazlıklara sunduğu çözümleri tartışabilme
components: a) Uluslararası birlikteliklerin anlaşmazlıklara sunduğu çözümlerle ilgili mantıksal temellendirme yapar.
b) Uluslararası birlikteliklerin anlaşmazlıklara sunduğu çözümlerle ilgili mantıksal tutarsızlık ve geçersizlikleri tespit eder.
c) Uluslararası birlikteliklerin anlaşmazlıklara sunduğu çözümleri kabul eder veya çürütür.

outcomes.text: Örnek ülkelerin ulaşım sistemlerini karşılaştırabilme
components: a) Örnek ülkelerin ulaşım sistemlerinin genel özelliklerini tanımlar.
b) Örnek ülkelerin ulaşım sistemlerinin benzerliklerini listeler.
c) Örnek ülkelerin ulaşım sistemlerinin farklılıklarını listeler.

outcomes.text: Örnek bir ülkeyi ticari faaliyetleri açısından sentezleyebilme
components: a) Örnek verilen ülkenin ticari faaliyetlerini belirler.
b) Örnek verilen ülke ile diğer ülkeler arasında ticari faaliyetler yönünden ilişki kurar.
c) Örnek verilen ülkenin ticari faaliyetlerine yönelik özgün bir ürün oluşturur.

outcomes.text: Örnek ülkelerin turizm faaliyetlerini karşılaştırabilme
components: a) Örnek ülkelerin turizm faaliyetlerinin genel özelliklerini tanımlar.
b) Örnek ülkelerin turizm faaliyetlerinin benzerliklerini listeler.
c) Örnek ülkelerin turizm faaliyetlerinin farklılıklarını listeler.

content: Tork
Denge
İtme (İmpuls) ve Momentum
Momentumun Korunumu
Eylemsizlik Momenti
Açısal Momentum

outcomes.text: Torkun matematiksel modeline yönelik tümevarımsal akıl yürütebilme
components: a) Torkun kuvvet, dönme noktasına uzaklık ve kuvvetin uygulama açısı ile ilişkisini matematiksel olarak modeller.
b) Torkun matematiksel modelini geneller.

outcomes.text: Denge, kütle merkezi ve ağırlık merkezi ile ilgili kanıt kullanabilme
components: a) Denge, kütle merkezi ve ağırlık merkezi ile ilgili verileri toplayarak kaydeder.
b) Denge, kütle merkezi ve ağırlık merkezi ile ilgili veri setleri oluşturur.
c) Denge, kütle merkezi ve ağırlık merkezi kavramlarını veriye dayalı olarak açıklar.

outcomes.text: İtme (İmpuls) ve momentum değişimi arasındaki ilişkiye yönelik bilimsel çıkarım yapabilme
components: a) İtme ve momentum değişimi arasındaki ilişkiye yönelik bileşenleri tanımlar.
b) İtme ve momentum değişimi arasındaki ilişkiye yönelik verileri toplayarak kaydeder.
c) İtme ve momentum değişimi arasındaki ilişkiye yönelik verileri yorumlar.

outcomes.text: Momentumun korunumunu veriye dayalı tahmin edebilme
components: a) Momentumun korunumuna ilişkin verileri toplar.
b) Veriler üzerinden momentumun korunumuna ilişkin hesaplamalar yapar.
c) Momentumun farklı uygulamalardaki korunumuna ilişkin yargıda bulunur.

outcomes.text: Eylemsizlik momentine yönelik tümevarımsal akıl yürütebilme
components: a) Eylemsizlik momentinin etkilerini birden fazla durumda gözlemler.
b) Eylemsizlik momentinin bağlı olduğu değişkenler ile ilişkisini bulur.
c) Eylemsizlik momentinin bağlı olduğu değişkenler ile ilişkisini geneller.

outcomes.text: Açısal momentumun korunumuna yönelik tümevarımsal akıl yürütebilme
components: a) Açısal momentumun bağlı olduğu değişkenleri gözlemler.
b) Açısal momentum ile bağlı olduğu değişkenler arasındaki ilişkiyi bulur.
c) Açısal momentumun korunumunu bağlı olduğu değişkenler üzerinden geneller.

units.subject: Fizik
conceptualSkills: KB2.16. Muhakeme (Akıl Yürütme) (KB2.16.1. Tümevarımsal Akıl Yürütme)
content: Yay Sabiti
Yayın Esneklik Potansiyel Enerjisi
Sürtünme Kuvvetinin Yaptığı İş
Enerjinin Korunumu
Verim

outcomes.text: Yay sabitini tanımlamak için deney yapabilme
components: a) Farklı yaylardaki kuvvet ve uzanım değişkenlerine göre yay sabitini bulabileceği bir deney tasarlar.
b) Farklı yaylar için kuvvet ve uzanım grafiklerini oluşturarak analiz eder.

outcomes.text: Yay sabitinin matematiksel modeline ilişkin tümevarımsal akıl yürütebilme
components: a) Yay sabitine ilişkin kuvvet ile uzanım değişkenleri arasındaki örüntüyü matematiksel olarak modeller.
b) Yay sabitine ilişkin oluşturulan matematiksel model üzerinden genelleme yapar.

outcomes.text: Yayın esneklik potansiyel enerjisinin matematiksel modeline ilişkin tümevarımsal akıl yürütebilme
components: a) Kuvvet-uzanım grafiğinden yararlanarak yayın esneklik potansiyel enerjisinin matematiksel modeline ulaşır.
b) Farklı veri setleri ile hesaplamalar yaparak yayın esneklik potansiyel enerjisinin matematiksel modelini geneller.

outcomes.text: Sürtünme kuvvetinin yaptığı işe yönelik tümevarımsal akıl yürütebilme
components: a) Sürtünme kuvvetinin yaptığı iş ile ilgili gözlem yapar.
b) Sürtünme kuvvetinin yaptığı işi matematiksel olarak modeller.
c) Sürtünme kuvvetinin yaptığı işi matematiksel modelden yararlanarak geneller.

outcomes.text: Enerjinin dönüşümü ve korunumuna ilişkin bilimsel çıkarım yapabilme
components: a) Enerjinin dönüşümü ve korunumuna ilişkin özellikleri tanımlar.
b) Enerjinin dönüşümü ve korunumuna ilişkin veri toplayarak kaydeder.
c) Enerjinin korunumunu matematiksel modelleri kullanarak yorumlar ve değerlendirir.

outcomes.text: Mekanik sistemlerin verimi ile ilgili tümevarımsal akıl yürütebilme
components: a) Mekanik sistemlerin verimi ile ilgili değişkenleri sistemden alınan enerji, sisteme verilen enerji olarak belirler.
b) Mekanik sistemlerin verimi ile ilgili değişkenlerin arasındaki ilişkiyi belirler.
c) Mekanik sistemlerin verimi ile ilgili hesaplamalar yaparak değişkenler arasındaki ilişkiyi geneller.

units.subject: Fizik

content: Su Dalgalarında Kırınım
Işıkta Kırınım
Su Dalgalarında Girişim
Işıkta Girişim
Elektromanyetik Dalgalar
Işık Renkleri
Mekanik veya Elektromanyetik Dalgaların Kullanıldığı Cihazlar

outcomes.text: Doğrusal su dalgalarında kırınım olayına ilişkin tümevarımsal akıl yürütebilme
components: a) Doğrusal su dalgalarında kırınım olayını gözlemler.
b) Doğrusal su dalgalarında kırınım olayını frekans, dalga boyu ve yarık genişliği değişkenleri ile ilişkilendirir.
c) Doğrusal su dalgalarında gerçekleşen kırınım olayına ilişkin genelleme yapar.

outcomes.text: Dairesel su dalgalarında girişim olayına ilişkin tümevarımsal akıl yürütebilme
components: a) Dairesel su dalgalarında girişim olayını gözlemler.
b) Dairesel su dalgalarında girişim olayını frekans, dalga boyu ve kaynaklar arası mesafe değişkenleri ile ilişkilendirir.
c) Dairesel su dalgalarında gerçekleşen girişim olayına ilişkin genelleme yapar.

outcomes.text: Işıkta girişim ile ilgili deney yapabilme
components: a) Işığın girişimi ile ilgili deney tasarlar.
b) Işığın girişimi ile ilgili deney düzeneğinden veri toplayarak analiz eder.

outcomes.text: Işıkta kırınım ile ilgili deney yapabilme
components: a) Işığın kırınımı ile ilgili deney tasarlar.
b) Işığın kırınımını deney düzeneğinden veri toplayarak analiz eder.

outcomes.text: Elektromanyetik dalgaları sınıflandırabilme
components: a) Elektromanyetik dalgaların niteliklerini belirler.
b) Elektromanyetik dalgaları niteliklerine göre ayrıştırır.
c) Elektromanyetik dalgaları niteliklerine göre gruplandırır.
ç) Elektromanyetik dalgaları adlandırır.

outcomes.text: Işık renklerinin dalga boyları hakkında tümevarımsal akıl yürütebilme
components: a) Işık renkleri ve dalga boyları arasındaki ilişkiyi bulur.
b) Tüm ışık renklerinin ana ışık renkleri ile ilişkisine yönelik genelleme yapar.

outcomes.text: Mekanik veya elektromanyetik dalgaların kullanıldığı cihazlardaki dalga türlerini sorgulayabilme
components: a) Mekanik veya elektromanyetik dalgaların kullanıldığı cihazlardan merak ettiği cihazı belirler.
b) Mekanik veya elektromanyetik dalgaların kullanıldığı cihazlardan merak ettiği cihaz hakkında sorular sorar.
c) Mekanik veya elektromanyetik dalgaların kullanıldığı cihazlardan merak ettiği cihaz ile ilgili bilgi toplar.
ç) Mekanik veya elektromanyetik dalgaların kullanıldığı cihazlardan merak ettiği cihaz ile ilgili topladığı bilgilerin doğru olup olmadığını değerlendirir.
d) Mekanik veya elektromanyetik dalgaların kullanıldığı cihazlardan merak ettiği cihaz ile ilgili topladığı bilgiler üzerinden çıkarım yapar.

units.subject: Fizik

content: Siyah Cisim Işıması
Fotoelektrik Etki
Yarı İletkenlik
Süper İletkenlik
Standart Model
Modern Atom Teorisi
Nükleer Enerji

outcomes.text: Planck sabitinin modern fiziğin doğuşundaki etkisini çözümleyebilme
components: a) Planck sabitinin modern fiziğin ortaya çıkışındaki etkisini siyah cisim ışıması olgusu üzerinden belirler.
b) Planck sabiti ile fotoelektrik etkinin ilişkisini belirler.

outcomes.text: Fotoelektrik etkinin bağlı olduğu koşullar ve foton kavramına ilişkin tümevarımsal akıl yürütebilme
components: a) Fotoelektrik etkinin bağlı olduğu değişkenleri gözlemler.
b) Fotoelektrik etkinin matematiksel modeline ulaşır.
c) Fotoelektrik etki ve foton kavramı arasındaki ilişkiyi geneller.

outcomes.text: Fotoelektrik etkinin uygulamaları ile ilgili sorgulama yapabilme
components: a) Fotoelektrik etkiyi tanımlar.
b) Fotoelektrik etki hakkında sorular sorar.
c) Fotoelektrik etkinin uygulamaları hakkında bilgi toplar.
ç) Fotoelektrik etkinin uygulamaları ile ilgili toplanan bilgilerin doğru olup olmadığını değerlendirir.
d) Fotoelektrik etkinin uygulamaları ile ilgili toplanan bilgiler üzerinde çıkarım yapar.

outcomes.text: Yarı iletkenlerin kullanım alanlarını ve önemini sorgulayabilme
components: a) Yarı iletkenleri tanımlar.
b) Yarı iletkenler hakkında sorular sorar.
c) Yarı iletkenler hakkında bilgi toplar.
ç) Yarı iletkenlerle ilgili toplanan bilgilerin doğru olup olmadığını değerlendirir.
d) Yarı iletkenlerle ilgili toplanan bilgiler üzerinden yarı iletkenlerin kullanım alanları ve önemine yönelik çıkarım yapar.

outcomes.text: Süper iletkenlerin kullanım alanlarını ve önemini sorgulayabilme
components: a) Süper iletkenleri tanımlar.
b) Süper iletkenler hakkında sorular sorar.
c) Süper iletkenler hakkında bilgi toplar.
ç) Süper iletkenlerle ilgili toplanan bilgilerin doğru olup olmadığını değerlendirir.
d) Süper iletkenlerle ilgili toplanan bilgiler üzerinden süper iletkenlerin kullanım alanları ve önemine yönelik çıkarım yapar.

outcomes.text: Standart modelin bileşenlerini çözümleyebilme
components: a) Standart modelde yer alan temel parçacıkları belirler.
b) Temel parçacıklar ve temel kuvvetler arasındaki ilişkileri belirler.

outcomes.text: Modern Atom Teorisi ile ilgili bilgileri yapılandırabilme
components: a) Atomun yapısındaki temel parçacıkları inceleyerek aralarındaki ilişkileri ortaya koyar.
b) Temel parçacıklarla ilgili bilgilerini kullanarak atomun yapısını ortaya koyar.

outcomes.text: Nükleer enerjiyi sorgulayabilme
components: a) Nükleer enerjiye ilişkin merak ettiği konuyu tanımlar.
b) Nükleer enerjiye ilişkin sorular sorar.
c) Nükleer enerji hakkında bilgi toplar.
ç) Nükleer enerjiye ilişkin bilgilerin doğruluğunu değerlendirir.
d) Nükleer enerjiye ilişkin toplanan bilgiler üzerinden çıkarımlar yapar.

b) Görsel sanatlarla ilgili mesleklerin benzerliklerini listeler.

content: Çok Figürlü Çizimlerle Kompozisyon Çalışması
Resim Yüzeyinde Renk İlişkileri ile Figürlü Kompozisyon Çalışması
Heykel ve Çevresel Düzeni ile İlgili Taslak Çalışması

outcomes.text: Çok figürlü çizimlerle kompozisyon oluşturabilme
components: a) Çok figürlü çizimlerle kompozisyon çalışmasına uygun görsel anlatım araçlarını belirler.
b) Çok figürlü çizimi kompozisyona dönüştürür.

outcomes.text: Renk ilişkileri ile çok figürlü kompozisyon oluşturabilme

content: SCHOOL LIFE, CLASSROOM LIFE AND EDUCATION
Sub-themes: ''Challenges and coping with challenges for success; graduation and future plans after school; national days and celebrations''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):
Vocabulary for challenges and coping with challenges for success:
Nouns: Stress management, challenge, a consequence, an element, excitement, importance, worry.
Verbs: To set goals, to concentrate, to graduate, to indicate.
Adjectives: Determined, ambitious, competitive, complex, confident, confused, disappointed, disappointing, effective.
Adverbs: Successfully, simply.
Vocabulary for graduation and future plans after school:
Nouns: A ceremony, a cap, passion, an application, a qualification, a recommendation, following, a strength, scholarship.
Verbs: To deliver a speech, to volunteer, to work part-time, to appreciate.
Adjectives: Pleasant, essential, expected, experienced.
Adverbs: Possibly, forever.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".

*(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Background Grammatical Structures in Use:
-The Simple Present Tense: (I write a blog twice a week).
-The Present Progressive Tense: (They are attending workshops this week).
-Be Going to Future Tense: (He is going to apply for a job tomorrow).
-The Simple Future Tense: (He will go to college next year).
*About “Background Grammatical Structures in Use”:

The “Background Grammatical Structures” in this section are not only revisional but also serve as contextual support and contribute to meaning-making. They are intended to be used within the theme to help students grasp the meaning of the language constructed through the use of “Target Grammatical Structures” without being explicitly taught. These structures are not considered "Target Grammatical Structures” themselves rather they function as a part of the facilitation process, supporting both the target forms and the contexts in which they are used. They provide opportunities for learning through revised and scaffolded language.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Reported Speech of the Present and Future Tenses: (He says he attended workshops. They told me that they would attend the graduation party).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of the Simple Present Tense: Describing a general state or habit for revision.
-Use of the Present Progressive Tense: Describing an action happening now or temporarily for revision.
-Use of ''Be going to'' future tense: Describing planned actions, decisions or predictions based on evidence for future revision.
-Use of the Simple Future Tense: Describing spontaneous decisions, promises, or predictions based on opinions for future revision.
-Use of Reported Speech of the Present and Future Tenses: Reporting actions, ideas or plans for present and future tenses.
-Use of verbs for reported speech: Ask, report, say, tell.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Who’s your reading buddy?
Let’s wrap this up!
Shall we take turns presenting?
We’re on the same page.
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Intonation for positive statements, negative statements, questions and question tags.
keyConcepts: The target concept of this theme ''school life

classroom life and education with its components such as challenges and coping with challenges for success; graduation and future plans after school'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their preexisting knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example
a student in an upper secondary school may know what ''school life
classroom life and education with its components such as challenges and coping with challenges for success; graduation and future plans after school'' means
but may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However
this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise
and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language

outcomes.text: Students can prepare and get ready for listening (to)/watching about the current content on ''school life, classroom life, and education with challenges and coping with challenges for success; graduation and future plans after school; national days and celebrations''.

d) Students make rational predictions about the current content by looking at the supplementary visual elements provided.

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-The Simple Past Tense: (They limited their social media usage.)
-The Past Progressive Tense: (She was jogging at seven o’clock yesterday.)
-The Past Perfect Tense: (They attended a wellness program after they had gone bankrupt.)
-The Past Perfect Progressive Tense: (She had been investing money for her future before she was in debt.)
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of the Simple Past Tense: Describing an action that was completed at a specific moment in the past for revision.
-Use of the Past Progressive Tense: Describing an action that was happening at a specific moment in the past.
-Use of the Past Perfect Tense: Describing an action that was completed before another action in the past for revision.
-Use of the Past Perfect Progressive Tense: Describing an action that was happening before another action in the past for revision.

content: CITY AND SOCIAL LIFE
Sub-themes: ''Different communities and lifestyles in the rural areas and cities; problems related to infrastructure and planning in the city and solutions''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):
Vocabulary for different communities and lifestyles in the rural areas and cities:
Nouns: Dairy products, a cultural event, a beauty centre, accommodation, childhood, a consumer, a countryside, a custom, financial issues, an immigrant, security, unemployment, youth, entertainment.
Verbs: To bake bread, to access, to afford, to benefit, to experience, to gather, to limit.
Phrasal verbs: To go up, to get around.
Adjectives: Central, criminal, economic, educated, far, grateful, retired, unemployed.
Adverb: Absolutely.
Vocabulary for problems related to infrastructure and planning in the city and solutions:
Nouns: A connection, lack of green spaces, high property prices, high energy demand, planning, power cuts, a development, an improvement, a pipe, a warning, waste.
Verbs: To improve safety, to expand (public transportation), to meet demands.
Adjectives: Alternative, unable, various.
Adverbs: Approximately, highly.

*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations: “29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".

*(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
The Future Perfect Tense: (By the end of the season, we will have harvested all the vegetables from the farm).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of the Future Perfect Tense: Describing actions that will be completed before a specified time in the future.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
The race was neck and neck until the very end!
The crowd went wild when the home team scored!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Vowel: i (/aı/, /ı/, /i:/)
Consonants: j (/dʒeɪ/, /dʒ/); k: (/k/); l: (/ɛl/; /l/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)
keyConcepts: The target concept of this theme ''city life and social life with its components such as different communities and lifestyles in the rural areas and cities; problems related to infrastructure and planning in the city and solutions'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example

a student in an upper secondary school may know what ''city life and social life with its components such as different communities and lifestyles in the rural areas and cities; problems related to infrastructure and planning in the city and solutions'' means
but may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However
this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise
and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language

fieldSkills: FLFS1. Listening/Watching-Comprehension FLFS2. Reading-Comprehension FLFS3. Speaking-Expression FLFS4. Writing-Expression FLSS1. Grammaring: Selection and Use FLSS2. Vocabulary: Selection and Use FLSS3. Pronunciation: Selection and Use
sel: SELS1.3. Self- Reflection Skill SELS2.1. Communication Skill
content: LIFE IN THE CULTURAL AND NATURAL WORLD
Sub-themes: ''Stereotypes and cultural diversity in the world; gaining awareness on climate change''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):
Vocabulary for stereotypes and cultural diversity in the world:
Nouns: An immigrant, a refugee, a cultural element, a similarity, poverty, a religion, a nation, a race, a native, stereotype.
Verbs: To represent, to risk.
Phrasal verbs: To get on well, to back up.
Adjectives: Obvious, political, religious, native, stereotypical.
Adverbs: Similarly, originally, specifically.
Vocabulary for gaining awareness on climate change:
Nouns: Climate emergency, global heating.
Verbs: To highlight climate issues, to engage with, to educate the community, to contact local representatives, to support green policies, to create awareness campaigns, to reduce emissions.
Adjectives: Aware of, open-minded.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".

*(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Modals in the past (can/would/could/should have v3): (People could have avoided prejudicing others if they had taken the time to learn about different cultures).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of modals in the past (can/would/could/should have v3): Describing possibility, probability, necessity and obligation in the past.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Learning about different cultures is the spice of life!
Don’t judge a book by its cover!
Cultural diversity makes the world more colourful!
The Earth is getting warmer!
Let’s do something before it’s too late!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Vowel: o: (/əʊ/, /ɒ/)
Consonants: m: (/ɛm/, /m/); n: (/ɛn/, /n/); p: (/piː/, /p/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)
keyConcepts: The target concept of this theme ''stereotypes and cultural diversity in the world; gaining awareness on climate change'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example
a student in an upper secondary school may know what ''stereotypes and cultural diversity in the world; gaining awareness on climate change'' means
but may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However
this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise
and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language

content: LIFE THE UNIVERSE AND THE FUTURE
Sub-themes: ''Space organisations; plans and aspirations for the future''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):
Vocabulary for space organisations:

Nouns: NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration), space habitat, space missions, an astronaut, a rocket, atmosphere, Mars, moonlight, a spaceship, space station, sunlight, mystery, wonder, TSA (Turkish Space Agency).
Verbs: To be responsible for, to be involved in, to collect samples, to shine, to reflect, to survive.
Vocabulary for plans and aspirations for the future:
Nouns: Contribution, a goal, career.
Verbs: To set goals, to pursue dreams, to accomplish, to contribute, to entertain, to improve, to achieve, to reach.
Phrasal verb: To come up with.
Adjectives: Bold, optimistic, realistic.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".

*(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Conditional 3: (If the space agency had received more funding, they would have been able to launch a new spacecraft this year).
-Mixed conditionals: (If the space tourism industry had made faster progress, commercial space flights would be more accessible today).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of the conditional 3: Expressing hypothetical or unreal situations in the past.
-Use of mixed conditionals: Expressing regrets about past decisions or criticism of past actions.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Building a colony on Venus feels like pie in the sky!
Space tourism is just around the corner!
My head’s full of ideas and I just need the right time!
I’m not there yet, but I’m getting closer every day!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Vowel: u: (/juː/, /ʌ/, /juː/)
Consonants: v: (/viː/, /v/); w: (/w/); x: (/ɛks/, /ks/, /gz/); y: (/waɪ/, /j/, /ɪ/, /iː/); z: /zed/ (Br), /ziː/ (AmE), /z/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)

a student in an upper secondary school may know what ''life in the universe and the future with its components such as space organisations; plans and aspirations for the future'' means
but may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However
this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise
and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language
plans and aspirations for the future.

outcomes.text: Students can prepare and get ready for listening (to)/watching about the current content on ''life in the universe and future with space organisations; plans and aspirations for the future''.

units.theme: Upper Secondary-Year 12 (After Prep)-Level: B2.4 - Theme 1: School Lıfe & Educatıon
content: SCHOOL LIFE AND EDUCATION
Sub-themes: "Challenges to be successful (to succeed); graduation from school; future plans after school; national days and celebrations''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):

Vocabulary for challenges to be successful: Nouns: An aspiration, a norm, a demand, a workaholic, a rival, an outcome, a burden, tension, promotion, a perception, a breakdown, an attendance. Verbs: To dedicate, to exceed, to prioritise, to sacrifice, to handle, to fulfil, to overload, to desire, to criticise, to absorb, to tackle, to cope. Adjectives: Ambitious, challenging, overwhelmed, demanding, diligent, compelled, harsh, consuming. Adverbs: Consistently, reasonably, accurately, constantly, strictly. Vocabulary for graduation from school: Nouns: A bachelor’s/master’s/doctorate degree, a diploma, a farewell, a ceremony, a reception, a cap, a milestone, an admission, a curriculum, honour, a registration. Verbs: To conclude, to gather, to apply, to implement. Adjectives: Proud, joyful, significant, memorable, moving. Vocabulary for future plans after school: Nouns: A prospect, an internship, a scholarship, an application, a resume, a path, an option, employment, a portfolio, entrepreneurship, an institution, a workplace, a probability, expertise, an asset, a placement. Verbs: To chase, to embrace, to explore, to establish, to pursue, to launch, to specialize, to proceed, to reckon, to recruit. Phrases: A higher education, a gap year, vocational training, to set goals. Adjectives: Optimistic, pessimistic, essential, inspiring, diverse, innovative, principal, probable. Adverbs: Subsequently, consequently, potentially.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”.

*(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:

-Revision of the Mixed (the Present and Perfect) Tenses: The Simple Present Tense, the Present Progressive Tense, the Present Perfect Tense, the Present Perfect Progressive Tense: (She has worked at the company for five years. She is starting her new position next week. I always eat dinner at 7:00 in the morning. I am meeting my friends at 8:00 pm).
-Passive Voice for/in Present Tenses for Daily Speech, Formal Situations and Written Correspondence: (The projects are completed on time by our team. Registration forms are applied at the reception).

-Linkers/Connectives of Contrast, Reason, Addition, Purpose, Result, Giving Examples) (However, nevertheless, because of, in spite of, and, so as to, thus, so, such as, etc.): (She was not able to go to school because of the weather conditions).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:

-Use of Revision of Mixed (the Present and the Future) Tenses: The Simple Present Tense, the Present Progressive Tense, the Present Perfect Tense, the Present Perfect Progressive Tense: Describing actions about daily routines, ongoing activities, past experiences with current relevance, and future events or plans for revision.

-Use of Passive Voice of the Present Tenses for Daily Speech, Formal Situations and Written Correspondence: Describing actions and events where the doer is not emphasised, focusing instead on the outcome or the object of the action in a more polite and objective way.

-Use of Linkers/Connectives of Contrast, Reason, Addition, Purpose, Result, Giving Examples) (However, nevertheless, because of, in spite of, and, so as to, thus, so, such as, etc.): Connecting ideas and showing relationships.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Knowledge is power!
Let’s set some goals for the term!
Let’s see what awaits us after graduation!
Don’t put all your eggs in one basket!

-Intonation for positive statements, negative statements, questions, and question tags.

content: CLASSROOM LIFE & LEARNING
Sub-themes: "Digital and collaborative projects; student-led class activities; academic skills for learning''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):

Vocabulary for academic skills for learning: Nouns: A draft, an outline, a passage, feedback, determination, imagination. Verbs: To interpret, to calculate, to cite. Adjectives: Comprehensive, literary, logical, curious, enthusiastic, flexible. Vocabulary for digital and collaborative projects: Nouns: A file, a document, a timeline, a deadline, a consensus, a resolution, a forum, a database. Verbs: To collaborate, to store, to share, to brainstorm, to submit, to assign, to generate, to distribute, to exchange, to measure, to reinforce, to negotiate, to integrate. Adjectives: Rewarding, efficient, cooperative, accountable, instant, sophisticated, innovative. Adverbs: Considerably, remarkably. Vocabulary for student-led class activities: Nouns: A participant, a debate, a reflection, a presentation, a concept, a topic, a workshop, a viewpoint, a framework, interaction, a pursuit. Verbs: To participate, to display, to take turns, to facilitate, to propose, to contribute, to assure, to strengthen, to undertake, to derive, to interact, to coordinate. Adjectives: Opposing, enriching, mutual, respectful, progressive, comprehensive.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:

-Revision of the Mixed (Past) Tenses: (The Simple Past Tense, the Past Progressive Tense, the Past Perfect Tense, the Past Perfect Progressive Tense) :(By the end of the class, they had strengthened their mutual understanding through comprehensive discussions. The participants were brainstorming solutions when the teacher assigned new tasks).
-Passive Voice of the Past Tenses for Daily Speech, Formal Situations and Written Correspondence: (The debate was facilitated by the students).

-Causatives (Past) (had + object + base verb) (have something done) (make/made, get/got, let/let, help/helped) + base form or past participle: (The headmaster had the teachers do the meeting. The teacher helped the students finish the project. The teacher got the project finished).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:

-Use of Revision of the Mixed (Past) Tenses: (The Simple Past Tense, the Past Progressive Tense, the Past Perfect Tense, the Past Perfect Progressive Tense): Revising mixed past events or action in different contexts.

-Use of Passive Voice of the Past Tenses for Daily Speech, Formal Situations and Written Correspondence: Describing past events when the focus is on the action or the object of the action, rather than the person performing the action.

-Use of Causatives (Past) (had + object + base verb) (have something done) (made, got, let, helped) + base form or past participle: Expressing that someone causes another person to do something rather than doing the work themselves.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Two heads are better than one! A stitch in time saves nine! Can we go over that problem again? That’s a brilliant idea-let’s build the project on it!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
-Intonation for positive statements, negative statements, questions, and question tags.
keyConcepts: The target concept of this theme ''classroom life and learning with its components such as digital and collaborative projects; student-led class activities; academic skills for learning'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example

a student in year 12 of upper secondary school may know what ''classroom life and learning with its components such as digital and collaborative projects; student-led class activities; academic skills for learning'' means but may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However
this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise
and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language

units.theme: Upper Secondary-Year 12 (After Prep)-Level: B2.4 - Theme 3: Personal Lıfe & Well-Beıng
content: PERSONAL LIFE & WELL-BEING
Sub-themes: "Technology (AI) and its impact on daily life; dealing with burnout and staying motivated''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):

Vocabulary for technology (AI) and its impact on daily life: Nouns: An intervention, automation, detection, a pattern, an assistant, assistance, transparency, a function, categorization. Verbs: To anticipate, to operate, to function, to forecast, to tailor, to categorize, to manipulate, to navigate, to mimic. Adjectives: Responsive, capable, transparent, autonomous. Adverbs: Consistently. Vocabulary for dealing with burnout and staying motivated: Nouns: Perspective, mindfulness, burnout, encouragement, stability, challange. Verbs: To concentrate, to handle, to distribute, to encourage, to approach, to overcome. Adjectives: Consistent, encouraging, mindful. Adverbs: Deliberately.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:

-Revision of the Mixed (Future) Tenses (Be Going to Future Tense, the Future Progressive Tense, the Future Perfect Tense, the Future Perfect Progressive Tense): (Artificial intelligence is going to forecast patterns in consumer behaviour soon. By 2030, most industries will have started using AI-powered systems).
-Passive Voice of the Future Tenses for Daily Speech, Formal Situations and Written Correspondence: (Mindfulness exercises will be introduced to employees to enrich their well-being).

-Time Expressions to Express the Future: (Tomorrow, next month, in two weeks, on Friday, this Saturday, at 5 o’clock, soon, later, by Monday, for, until, till, some day, one day, eventually, by next month, as soon as, when, after, once).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:

-Use of Revision of the Mixed (Future) Tenses (Be Going to Future Tense, the Future Progressive Tense, the Future Perfect Tense, the Future Perfect Progressive Tense): Describing intentions, ongoing actions, completed events, sequential activities, or continuous processes relative to a specific time in future.

-Use of Passive Voice of the Future Tenses for Daily Speech, Formal Situations and Written Correspondence: Describing actions or processes in terms of their outcomes or effects to emphasise what will be done, achieved, or impacted in future contexts.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Every cloud has a silver lining!
A healthy mind is in a healthy body!
I’m finally back on my feet!
Let’s talk about what’s been bothering you?
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
-Intonation for positive statements, negative statements, questions, and question tags.
keyConcepts: The target concept of this theme ''personal life and well-being with its components such as technology (AI) and its impact on daily life; dealing with burnout and staying motivated'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example

a student in year 12 of upper secondary school may know what ''personal life and well-being with its components such as technology (AI) and its impact on daily life; dealing with burnout and staying motivated'' mean but may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However
this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise
and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language

content: FAMILY LIFE & HOME
Sub-themes: "Maintaining relationship with family members; challenges of modern societies for families''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):

Vocabulary for maintaining relationship with family members: Nouns: Harmony, trust, loyalty, commitment, forgiveness, sympathy, transparency, consideration, sincerity, appreciation. Verbs: To bond, to reunite, to appreciate, to forgive, to commit, to forgive. Adjectives: Supportive, respectful, trustworthy, loyal, considerate, sincere. Adverbs: Supportively, sincerely. Vocabulary for challenges of modern societies for families: Nouns: Complexity, hardship, isolation, conflict, exhaustion, insecurity, overload. Verbs: To shift (the roles), to diversify, to constraint, to handle, to prompt, to provoke, to reconcile, to encounter. Adjectives: Exhausted, reluctant. Adverbs: Competitively, rapidly, reluctantly. Phrases: Technological dependence, internal or external conflicts, financial collapse, lack of resources, global crises.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Background Grammatical Structures in Use:

-Revision of the Mixed (All Present and Perfect) Tenses: (Forgiveness plays a significant role in relationships. I am considering how to be more supportive of my family during tough times. We have encountered many challenges. The family has struggled with financial instability).
*About “Background Grammatical Structures in Use”:

The “Background Grammatical Structures” in this section are not only revisional but also serve as contextual support and contribute to meaning-making. They are intended to be used within the theme to help students grasp the meaning of the language constructed through the use of “Target Grammatical Structures” without being explicitly taught. These structures are not considered “Target Grammatical Structures” themselves rather they function as a part of the facilitation process, supporting both the target forms and the contexts in which they are used. They provide opportunities for learning through revised and scaffolded language.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:

-Reported Speech of the Present and Perfect Tenses for Daily Speech, Formal Situations and Written Correspondence: (The expert says that trust is the foundation of every relationship. The therapist states that loyalty among people is crucial for cooperation. I am writing to inform you that financial collapse is the main topic of our meeting).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:

-Use of Reported Speech of the Present and Perfect Tenses for Daily Speech, Formal Situations and Written Correspondence with different Reporting verbs: say, tell, ask, state, report, announce, declare, explain, wonder, suggest, propose, agree, disagree, conclude, etc.: Reporting what someone else has said or shared about present situations, ongoing actions, or recent experiences in a more polite and objective way. -Use of Revision of the Mixed (All Present and Perfect) Tenses: Describing actions about daily routines, ongoing activities, past experiences with current relevance.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Charity begins at home!
Let’s have a family meeting to sort this out!
Films about families hit close to home!
Everybody’s here. It’s all in the family!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Vowels: a, e
Consonants: b, c, d
Vowels: a: (/ae/, /aeı/, /ə/, /a:/, /eɪ/, /a:/, /a/, /ɔː/, /eə/); e: (/e/; /i:/, /ə/, silent /e/)
Consonant: b: (/b/), silent /b/); c: (/si/, /k/, /tʃ/, /z/, silent /c/); d: (/d/), silent /d/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme).
keyConcepts: The target concept of this theme ''family life and home with its components such as maintaining relationship with family members; challenges of modern societies for families'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example

a student in year 12 of upper secondary school may know what ''family life and home with its components such as maintaining relationship with family members; challenges of modern societies for families'' means but may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However
this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise
and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language
challenges of modern societies for families.

components: a) Students listen to, watch, and/or read the audio, visual, and written current content presented in context that introduces the general use of the target language structures in the current theme.

content: LIFE IN THE NEIGHBOURHOOD, CITY, AND SOCIAL LIFE
Sub-themes: "Architecture and design in cities; volunteerism in social communities''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):

Vocabulary for architecture and design in cities: Nouns: Concrete, construction, creation, urbanisation. Verbs: To stand out, to construct, to elevate, to refurbish. Adjectives: Interior, exterior, daring, iconic, lively, elegant, unique, outstanding, classic. Adverbs: Constantly, elegantly, boldly. Vocabulary for volunteerism in social communities: Nouns: A volunteer, a charity, fundraising, an initiative, engagement, empathy. Verbs: To lead, to advocate, to inspire, to mentor, to coordinate, to extend, to engage, to dedicate, to captivate. Adjectives: Non-profit, dedicated, inspirational, passionate, captivating. Adverbs: Diligently.

A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.

-Reported Speech of the Past Tenses for Daily Speech, Formal Situations and Written Correspondence: (She said that she had joined a charity organisation voluntarily. The charity director stated in the email that their non-profit organisation had raised enough funds for the community centre renovation).
Background Grammatical Structures in Use:

-Revision of the Mixed (Past) Tenses (The Simple Past Tense, the Past Progressive Tense, the Past Perfect Tense, the Past Perfect Progressive Tense): (By the time the charity event started, the volunteers had already set up the venue. The committee had already completed the renovation when the mayor announced the new deadline for the project).

They provide opportunities for learning through revised and scaffolded language.

units.theme: Upper Secondary-Year 12 (After Prep)-Level: B2.4 - Theme 6: Lıfe In The World & Culture
content: LIFE IN THE WORLD & CULTURE
Sub-themes: "The influence of technology on cultural habits; the role of education in preserving culture''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):
Vocabulary for the influence of technology on cultural habits: Nouns: An artefact. Verbs: To replace, to reshape, to integrate, to archive, to blend. Adjectives: Accessible, dynamic. Adverbs: Firmly.

Vocabulary for the role of education in preserving culture: Nouns: A commitment, a core, a generation, a heritage. Verbs: To time, to incorporate, to foster, to convey, to facilitate. Adjectives: Crucial, comprehensive, consistent. Adverbs: Thus.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”.

*(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Background Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Can for Probability: (Artificial intelligence can increase the efficiency of cultural archiving systems).
-Could for Probability: (A sudden increase in the number of views could indicate that a video will go viral).
-May, Might for Probability: (Education reforms may/might have lasting effect).

-Could for Deduction or Speculation: (The fingerprints on the artefact could belong to primitive people native to the area). -Need for Necessity: (Schools need to encourage young people to value cultural heritage).
-Needn’t for Lack of Obligation: (We needn’t bring our laptop to the meeting; they will provide all the necessary devices).
-Must vs Have to: (We must archive these cultural artefacts to preserve our cultural heritage. We have to archive these cultural artefacts because the legislation requires it).
-Should for Advice: (We should integrate cultural heritage into the curriculum to provide a deeper understanding among students).

-Must/Can’t for Deduction: (Education must be a crucial factor in passing down cultural heritage, as it facilitates consistent learning across generations. This artefact can’t be purely handmade because the blending of materials cannot be done without technology).
*About “Background Grammatical Structures in Use”:

The “Background Grammatical Structures” in this section are not only revisional but also serve as contextual support and contribute to meaning-making. They are intended to be used within the theme to help students grasp the meaning of the language constructed through the use of “Target Grammatical Structures” without being explicitly taught. These structures are not considered “Target Grammatical Structures” themselves rather they function as a part of the facilitation process, supporting both the target forms and the contexts in which they are used. They provide opportunities for learning through revised and scaffolded language.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
Modals:

-Reported Speech of Modals for Daily Speech, Formal Situations and Written Correspondence: (Experts say that technology can reshape how people interact with each other. They say that we must convey a consistent understanding of cultural values to the next generation).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of Reported Speech of Modals for Daily Speech, Formal Situations and Written Correspondence: Reporting modal verbs in speech and writing.
-Use of Can for Probability: Expressing that something is possible/probable under normal circumstances. -Use of Could for Probability: Expressing that something is possible but not certain.
-Use of May, Might for Probability: Expressing that something is possible but not certain.
-Use of Could for Deduction or Speculation: Expressing that something is possible or might be true, based on available evidence or logical reasoning. -Use of Need for Necessity: Expressing necessity.
-Use of Needn’t for Lack of Obligation: Expressing lack of obligation.

-Use of Must vs Have to: Discriminating between expressing a strong internal or personal obligation, often with urgency, and expressing an external obligation imposed by rules, laws, or circumstances.
-Use of Should for Giving Advice: Offering suggestions or recommendations. -Use of Must/Can’t for Deduction: Expressing a strong positive or negative deduction based on evidence or reasoning.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Istanbul is truly a melting pot of cultures.
That is a tradition passed down from generation to generation!
We must keep our culture alive!
Variety is the spice of life.
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Vowel: o
Consonants: l, m, n, (ng), p
Vowel: o: (/əʊ/, /ɒ/, /əʊ/)
Consonants: l: (/ɛl/ /l/, silent /l/); m; (/ɛm/,/m/); n: (/ɛn/, /n/, silent /n/); ng: (/ng/); p: (piː//p/, silent /p/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme).

Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example

a student in year 12 of upper secondary school may know what ''the influence of technology on cultural habits; the role of education in preserving culture'' means but may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However
this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise
and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language

units.theme: Upper Secondary-Year 12 (After Prep)-Level: B2.4 - Theme 7: Lıfe In Nature & Global Problems
content: LIFE IN NATURE & GLOBAL PROBLEMS
Sub-themes: "Natural disaster prevention, preparedness and balancing; eco-systems; eco-tourism and responsible travel''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):

Vocabulary for natural disaster prevention, preparedness and balancing; eco-systems: Nouns: A threat, a construction, a defence, a measure, a kit, an aid, a shelter, coordination, biodiversity, a survivor. Verbs: To construct, to alarm, to back, to defend, to strike, to detect, to undergo, to survive. Phrases: Be subject to smt., food chain. Adjectives: Collaborative, flexible, preventive, destructive, devastating, surrounding. Adverbs: Truly, thoroughly, emotionally. Vocabulary for eco-tourism and responsible travel: Nouns: A commission, well-being, sensitivity, an impact, a destination, theft. Verbs: To trouble, to urge, to conserve, to host, to minimise, to enhance, to undertake, to oppose. Adjectives: Acceptable, offensive, voluntary, appropriate. Adverbs: Thus, otherwise. Phrases: Leave no trace, waste management.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”.

*(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Modals in the Past: (The evacuation should have been carried out earlier to save more lives).
-Passive Voice of Modals in the Past for Daily Speech, Formal Situations and Written Correspondence: (More precautions should have been taken to protect the city from natural disasters).

-Reported Speech of Modals in the Past for Daily Speech, Formal Situations and Written Correspondence: (The experts explained that the aid could have been distributed faster if the roads hadn’t been blocked).
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of Modals in the Past: Expressing past possibilities, obligations, and regrets.

-Use of Passive Voice of Modals in the Past for Daily Speech, Formal Situations and Written Correspondence: Expressing probability, deduction, speculation, necessity and obligation when the focus is on the action rather than the doer in a more formal or polite way.
-Use of Reported Speech of Modals in the Past for Daily Speech, Formal Situations and Written Correspondence: Reporting past ability, suggestion, obligation or assumption.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Every little bit helps!
Make hay while the sun shines!
You reap what you sow!
Let’s organise a clean-up event!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Vowel: u
Consonants: q, r, s, t
Vowel: u: (/juː/, /ʌ/, /juː/, silent /u/)
Consonants: q: (/kjuː/, /k/); r: (/ɑː/(Br), silent /r/ (Br), /aɹ/ (AmE), /ɹ/ (AmE), silent /r/ (Br)); s: (/s/, /ɛs/, /z/, silent /s/); t : (/tiː/, /t/, silent /t/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme).
keyConcepts: The target concept of this theme ''natural disaster prevention

preparedness and balancing; eco-systems; eco-tourism and responsible travel'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example
a student in year 12 of upper secondary school may know what ''natural disaster prevention

preparedness and balancing; eco-systems; eco-tourism and responsible travel'' means but may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However
this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise
and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language

units.theme: Upper Secondary-Year 12 (After Prep)-Level: B2.4 - Theme 8: Lıfe In The Unıverse & The Future
content: LIFE IN THE UNIVERSE & FUTURE
Sub-themes: "Future myths and legends; future of humanity''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):

Vocabulary for future myths and legends: Nouns: A folklore, a plot, a figure, a tale. Verbs: To represent, to symbolize, to reflect. Adjectives: Supernatural, heroic, courageous, spiritual. Vocabulary for future of humanity: Nouns: An assumption, a retirement, a principle, an advancement, a citizen. Verbs: To surround, to target, to elect, to found, to surpass, to collaborate, to investigate. Adjectives: Genuine, progressive, innovative, eco-friendly, digital, adaptive. Adverbs: Hopefully.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:

“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, “Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)”, “Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)”. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:

-Mixed Conditionals: (If you go to the Moon, everything floats in space. If a planet is in orbit, it travels around a star. If we find extraterrestrial life, it will be in a distant galaxy. If you want to explore space, you can be an astronaut. If citizens had collaborated to find solutions on environmental problems, we would be living in a more eco-friendly world today).
-Inversions: (In Conditional 3 and Mixed Conditionals): Had he taken the job in NASA, he would now be working on space missions.
Functions of the Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of Mixed Conditionals: Describing past unreal conditionals with present or future results.
-Use of Inversions: (In Conditional 3 and Mixed Conditionals): Expressing formality, emphasis, or stylistic variation by reversing the usual word order in conditional sentences.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Cross that bridge when you come to it!
Tomorrow is another day!
Let’s imagine a better world!
We need to look to the future!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Consonants: v, w, x, y, z
Consonants: v: (/viː/, /v/); w: (/w/), silent /w/); x: (/ɛks/, /ks/, /gz/); y: (/waɪ/, /j/, /ɪ/, /iː/); z: /(zed/ (Br), /ziː/ (AmE), /z/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme).
keyConcepts: The target concept of this theme ''life in the universe and the future with its components such as future myths and legends; future of humanity'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example

a student in year 12 of upper secondary school may know what ''life in the universe and the future with its components such as future myths and legends; future of humanity'' means but may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However
this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise
and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language
